18.t: Working with data: heating different materials
q: Which material had the biggest temperature rise?
Use c = E / (m × ΔT) to calculate c for copper.
Calculate c for water and compare it with aluminium.
9000 / 2.1 = about 4300 J/(kg °C), nearly five times aluminium’s 900.
Explain why a hot-water bottle uses water, not copper.
Water has a much higher c, so the same mass stores far more energy for each degree and releases it slowly.
The water value is a little higher than the data book (4200). Suggest why.
Some heater energy was lost to the air and container, so less than 9000 J went into the water; using 9000 J in the equation makes c look too big.
